gap: No result ChatGPT got states that DJI is the only maker in this set to put a duration on its overload rating: the US 120 V DJI Power 1000 (DYM1000L) holds 2,600 W for 30 s at 25 °C and 50% charge, while its 4,400 W 'peak' and the OUPES Mega 1's 4,500 W 'surge' have no duration at all. It also doesn't state that BLUETTI's own US pages give the Elite 30 V2 and Elite 100 V2 only a 'Lifting Power' figure (1,500 W / 2,700 W) and no surge figure, so ChatGPT's 158 W/lb for the Elite 30 V2 comes from a Lifting number, not a surge number.
standout_why: I compared against Volt & Valley's best-of-2026 page (cited) and Tested Watts' C1000 Gen 2 vs DELTA 3 Plus and Elite 100 V2 vs DELTA 3 Plus pages (both cited). None gives a surge or overload duration for any product. All three say their only ms figures are UPS switchover times. Volt & Valley puts the Elite 30 V2 in its table as '1,500W surge', but its body text calls the same figure 'Power Lifting', so that rival has part of the BLUETTI point. None of them has DJI's timed 2,600 W / 30 s figure. ChatGPT's own caveat says 'surge duration ... matter[s]' but gives no duration.
decides: This changes the shortlist rather than naming a final winner. The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 should come off the surge-per-pound table, because BLUETTI publishes no surge rating for it, only 1,500 W Lifting Power. The DJI Power 1000 becomes the only pick whose overload is backed by a stated time and test conditions: 2,600 W for 30 s from about 28.7 lb is about 91 W/lb for a held overload. OUPES's 4,500 W and DJI's 4,400 W are peak figures with no stated duration, so ChatGPT's 162 vs 153 W/lb ranking compares two unverified numbers. The page's footnote should say: only DJI tells you how long; nobody tells you how long the peak lasts.

findings.label: Timed overload (US 120 V model DYM1000L)
findings.note: Footnote **: 'At an output power of 2600 W, the DYM1000L prototype can sustain for 30 seconds, and the DYM1000H prototype can sustain for 60 seconds.' Measured at about 25 °C (77 °F) and 50% battery; DJI says duration varies with temperature and charge. I'm inferring that DYM1000L is the 120 V/US unit from the L/H naming and the page's region note. 2,600 W / 28.66 lb (13 kg × 2.2046) = 90.7 W/lb.

findings.label: Peak output (no duration stated)
findings.note: Spec reads 'peak output: 4400 W' with no time window. 4,400 / 28.66 lb = 153.5 W/lb, which matches ChatGPT's 153.

findings.label: Continuous and max total AC output
findings.note: 2,200 W continuous 'until the battery runs out' at 25 °C. Bypass (UPS passthrough) on DYM1000L is 1,440 W. The Japanese version is limited to 2,000 W continuous.

findings.label: Weight and volume
findings.note: Volume = 44.8 × 22.5 × 23.0 cm = 23,184 cm³. Timed overload per litre: 2,600 / 23.2 = 112 W/L.

The 3,600 W surge, 2,200 W X-Boost and 27.6 lb figures appear only on rival pages (Tested Watts).

Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 surge rating and any duration from the maker: anker.com and ankersolix.com product URLs returned 404, and the storecheck search on anker.com returned 404. I didn't open the Amazon listing.

BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 3,600 W surge in a maker document: the official BLUETTI support PDF (s4.bluettipower.com/.../4bacc59f...pdf) came back as compressed binary that WebFetch couldn't read, and the manuals.plus mirror returned 403. Search results show a Best Buy title saying '3600W peak', which I didn't open.
OUPES Mega 1 surge duration and test conditions: no figure in the store listing, and the maker's spec page returned HTTP 429.

A named reviewer's measured motor-start or peak-watt test for the OUPES Mega 1 or DJI Power 1000: thesolarlab.com's Mega 1 review says the unit 'pulls voltage during these types of surges' but names no reviewer, appliance or measured figure, so I left it out. I didn't open the batteryskills.com and bobvila.com reviews.
